body:
WHAT
PushNotification shows a desktop toast to the human (Windows toast via PowerShell, osascript on macOS, notify-send on Linux) with the message cut to 200 characters. The message is passed as an argument or environment variable, never spliced into a shell string. If delivery fails, the tool returns a plain note saying so; it never returns isError and never throws.

WHY
Without it the agent cannot get the user's attention when a long task finishes, and a failing notifier on a headless system would otherwise break the turn.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/pushNotification.ts — pushNotificationTool (permissionClass 'interact', status literal 'proactive'), MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS, execute() (slice + deliver + non-error result either way), deliver() platform switch, run() (execFile with 10s timeout, resolves false on error), runWindows() (message via env MAGENTRA_NOTIFY_MSG), appleScriptString().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Stub child_process.execFile to call back with an Error; execute { message:'hi', status:'proactive' }; assert the promise resolves, isError is undefined and content contains 'could not be delivered' and the message.
2. Stub execFile to succeed; assert content is 'Notification sent: "hi"'.
3. Pass a 300-char message; assert the message handed to execFile (or the env var on win32) is exactly 200 chars.
4. Pass a message containing a double quote and '$(rm -rf x)'; assert it reaches execFile only as an argument/env value and no shell string containing it is built (on darwin the AppleScript string has the quote escaped).
5. inputSchema.safeParse({ message:'x', status:'urgent' }) fails and with empty message fails.
